Question: What is the number of ordered triples \((a, b, c)\) of positive integers, with \(a \le b \le c \le 9,\) such that there exists a (non-degenerate) triangle \(\triangle ABC\) with an integer inradius for which \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are the lengths of the altitudes from \(A\) to \(\overline{BC},\) \(B\) to \(\overline{AC},\) and \(C\) to \(\overline{AB},\) respectively? (Recall that the inradius of a triangle is the radius of the largest possible circle that can be inscribed in the triangle.)
